name: Odile Brennagh
place: port town of Saint-Varre, the cholera year
cause: the same fever, in the ward she ran
summary: Infirmary nurse, formerly of a nursing order. Remained in the fever ward when the physicians left. Gave fatal doses of laudanum to nine patients she judged past saving.

entries.text: Nursed some three hundred through the epidemic after the physicians fled.
Ended nine lives with laudanum, without their consent or anyone's authority.
Lied to the magistrate's inquest about the nine.
Gave her wages to the children of the dead.
Left her order in 1829; reason not recorded.

hidden.text: One of the nine was recovering; she misjudged him.

archive.title: Ward physician's last daybook
cards: Dr. Hallam, Saint-Varre infirmary: last entry before he left the town.
Bed 7, Anselm Roche, carter: 'fever broken, will live.'
The nurse's list of the nine, found later: Roche is the seventh name.

fact.text: Anselm Roche, the seventh of her nine, was recovering.

answer: Because I had sat with the other three hundred. I knew what the last day looked like.
I would not make them have it.
questions.card: Knew what the last day looked like; would not make them have it.

fact.text: She spared the dying a last day she had watched three hundred times.

questions.text: Did any of them ask you to?
answer: Two did. The rest could not speak. I decided for them.
I have never pretended otherwise, except to the magistrate.
questions.card: Two asked. She decided for the other seven.

fact.text: Seven of the nine never asked; she decided for them.

answer: ...No. He was grey. He was... the daybook says that?
Then I killed a man who would have gone home. Write that down exactly as I said it.
questions.card: Accepts she killed a man who would have gone home. Asks it be written.

fact.text: Accepted the charge the moment she saw the daybook.

heaven: Anselm Roche is already there. He has asked not to be seated near her.
Some time later, he asks where she is.
hell: She asks the Warden whether Roche's family was ever told.
It is the first question the Warden has not had a form for.

ext.mitigating: Alone, unsupported, no physician to consult; acted to spare suffering; accepts the charge the moment she sees it.
